problem: `g.user["role"] not in roles` checks for a substring because the only caller passes a str (`require_role("admin")`). The empty role that `load_session` now gives unverified users is a substring of every string, so the check passes.
failure: Send `POST /admin/purge` with `X-Auth-Token: t-new` (an unverified `user`). `load_session` sets role "", and `"" in "admin"` is True, so there is no 403 and `purge()` runs. An unverified account gets admin access.
fix: Turn `roles` into a set in the decorator, e.g. `roles = frozenset([roles]) if isinstance(roles, str) else frozenset(roles)`, or reject a str outright.

problem: The call site was not updated for the new `roles` parameter. It still passes the bare string "admin", so any role that is a substring of "admin" is allowed.
failure: Any account whose role is "", "a", "ad", "adm" or "min" gets past `@require_role("admin")` and can call `POST /admin/purge`.
fix: Change it to `@require_role({"admin"})`, or normalize the str inside `require_role`.

problem: `require_role` does not check or normalize the type of `roles`. A str is accepted silently and so is any iterable or container, so each caller decides what `in` means.
failure: `require_role("editor")` passes for a role "edit". `require_role(None)` raises TypeError and returns 500 on every request.
fix: Normalize to a frozenset, wrapping a single str first, or raise TypeError when given a str.

problem: Using the empty string "" to mean "no role" is a value that membership and equality checks can match. This is what lets unverified accounts through the substring check.
failure: `"" in "admin"` is True, so an unverified user (`t-new`) gets through `require_role("admin")` and `/admin/purge` returns 200.
fix: Use `None` for the role, or keep the role and check `g.user["verified"]` explicitly in `require_role`.
